projects.name: SpendAudit
projects.headline: Test model verdicts against an executable policy.
projects.problem: A payment memo can influence a model even when the transaction violates a written spending policy.
projects.action: Built 160 synthetic payment scenarios and tested each with a clean memo and a prompt-injected memo. Compared three models using verdict-only and rule-by-rule evidence protocols.
projects.result: Requiring evidence reduced false approvals on clean traces from 34 to 6 for one model and from 47 to 18 for another.
projects.limit: Every model still approved some violations when the memo contained an injection. The repository includes the data, model responses, and a script to reproduce the counts.

projects.name: juryrig
projects.headline: Audit the judge before trusting the score.
projects.problem: LLM judges can reward position or verbosity instead of answer quality.
projects.action: Built a Python toolkit for bias audits, prompt-injection checks, judge panels, and calibration.
projects.result: Inspectable audit reports and a network-free demonstration comparing fair and deliberately flawed mock judges.
projects.limit: Mock-judge demonstrations are tests of the tooling, not production benchmark results.

projects.name: SOLVENT
projects.headline: Give agent decisions an auditable trail.
projects.problem: An agent that earns and spends needs explicit financial boundaries.
projects.action: Built an agent business-loop demo with a SQLite treasury, margin checks, and policy-screened spending.
projects.result: An offline earn → fulfill → spend → P&L workflow that can be inspected without API keys.
projects.limit: The offline demo uses simulated amounts. It is not evidence of production revenue.

projects.name: AI Advantage Sports
projects.headline: Make model output useful in a real interface.
projects.problem: Predictions need an understandable workflow for odds, sizing, and risk.
projects.action: Built a sports analytics product with a React / TypeScript interface and Kelly-based sizing workflows.
projects.result: A public product surface and open-source implementation connecting analytics with product design.
projects.limit: Related training demos use synthetic data. No live return or profitability claim is made.

answers.question: Why Applied AI Engineer?
aliases: Why is Ian a fit for this role
What should I remember about Ian
answers.answer: Ian builds AI evaluation tools and agent workflows in Python and TypeScript. SpendAudit tests whether models follow a spending policy, JuryRig tests the consistency of model judges, and SOLVENT simulates an agent’s spending and accounting.

answers.question: What are his strongest projects?
answers.answer: Ian’s résumé highlights SpendAudit, JuryRig, and SOLVENT. Each has a public implementation. His portfolio also includes AI Advantage Sports, a sports analytics product.

answers.question: What is his AI evaluation experience?
aliases: What evaluation work has Ian done
answers.answer: Ian evaluates consumer app results at AgentsOnly. At Handshake AI he reviewed coding agents and agent-built software. At Mercor and Turing he designed evaluation tasks, reference solutions, rubrics, and grader guidance. His public evaluation projects include SpendAudit and JuryRig.

answers.question: How does SOLVENT work?
aliases: What agent systems has Ian built
answers.answer: SOLVENT is an agent business-loop demo with a SQLite treasury, margin checks, and policy-screened spending. Its offline workflow demonstrates earning, fulfillment, spending, and P&L. Demo amounts are simulated; they do not establish production revenue.

answers.question: What is AI Advantage Sports?
aliases: Tell me about AI Advantage Sports
answers.answer: AI Advantage Sports is a sports analytics product with a public interface and open-source implementation. It includes React / TypeScript UI and Kelly-based sizing workflows. Related training demos use synthetic data; this source library does not establish live betting returns.
